blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: As pretraining scales, medical language models have advanced rapidly in clinical question answering. Their ability to achieve effective physiological control through sustained intervention still lacks systematic quantitative evaluation. Type 1 diabetes provides a concrete setting: impaired insulin secretion creates dependence on exogenous insulin, with dosing continually adjusted using information about meals, exercise, illness, and glucose measurements. We introduce DiabAgent, a research suite for agentic physiological control comprising the Agentic Physiological Control (APC) framework, the DiabetSim simulator, and the SweetBench benchmark. APC controls glucose through medical-device tools, using ongoing observations to infer individual states, accumulate personal experience, and choose treatment actions. We build DiabetSim to simulate different patients, events, and device conditions for scalable virtual testing and training. Using DiabetSim, we construct SweetBench by instantiating 32 scenario designs as 212 glucose-control tasks. With Claude Opus 5.5 and a fixed decision interval of one hour, APC achieves a COGI of 73.5, compared with 71.2 for the open-source closed-loop baseline OpenAPS. Ablations further show that individual adaptation and contextual information improve glucose control. Combining high-frequency rule-based control with lower-frequency agent decisions shows potential for balancing control performance and computational cost. Our work provides a framework, simulator, and evaluation foundation for agents to participate in human physiological control.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
As pretraining scales, medical language models have advanced rapidly in clinical question
answering and treatment advice ( Singhal et al., 2023 ; Arora et al., 2025 ) . Agents combine language
models with tools, memory, and environment feedback to execute multi-step
tasks ( Yao et al., 2023 ; Shinn et al., 2023 ) . They complete long tasks in software and service
environments and reuse experience in later decisions ( Yang et al., 2024 ; Yao et al., 2024 ; Zhao et al., 2024 ) .
Medical agents conduct diagnostic dialogue, analyze
treatment options, and operate electronic health
records ( Tu et al., 2025 ; Gao et al., 2025 ; Jiang et al., 2025 ) . Evaluation of these tasks
primarily concerns responses or information operations. Assessing whether language models
can control physiology through sustained intervention requires systematic evaluation of
the resulting physiological trajectories.

blocks.en:
Type 1 diabetes provides a concrete setting for this problem. People with type 1 diabetes
have impaired insulin secretion and depend on exogenous insulin for glucose control.
Dosing needs vary with meals, exercise, illness, and individual states, while insulin
continues to act for hours, linking current decisions to earlier treatment and subsequent
events ( Holt et al., 2021 ; Riddell et al., 2017 ) . Differences between people, daily
changes in insulin needs, and delayed, noisy, or missing glucose measurements make
control a long-horizon task requiring ongoing state inference, treatment adjustment,
and feedback tracking. Automated insulin delivery and learned closed-loop controllers
have advanced glucose control ( Brown et al., 2019 ; Sherr et al., 2022 ; Hettiarachchi et al., 2024 ; Sarkar, 2026 ) .
Existing dynamical models and evaluation metrics also provide a basis for simulating
glucose dynamics and assessing control outcomes ( Deichmann et al., 2023 ; Battelino et al., 2019 ) .
Together, these conditions support systematic study of how agents combine contextual
information, personal experience, and device tools for sustained physiological control.

blocks.en:
Rule-based closed-loop control typically organizes dosing around structured glucose
measurements, insulin records, carbohydrate estimates, and prescribed therapy
parameters ( OpenAPS community, 2026 ) . Using descriptions of a changed meal plan, illness recovery,
or a device problem requires mapping them to predefined inputs and response rules.
This mapping constrains how the controller can use cues in free-text context and personal
treatment notes. Interacting rare events and individual differences also require judging
which cues explain current glucose changes and subsequent dosing
needs ( Holt et al., 2021 ) . Can an agent interpret this context and personal experience, act through medical-device
tools, and translate that understanding into better physiological control? This question motivates the Agentic Physiological Control ( APC ) framework
that we study in DiabAgent .

blocks.en:
APC treats treatment as a control problem in which the controller is an agent and the
sensors and actuators are medical devices.

measure and act on it, reports from the person, and a score on the physiological trajectory.

blocks.en: 2.2 Glucose Control
blocks.zh: 2.2 葡萄糖管制

blocks.en:
Rule-based glucose controllers organize dosing around structured glucose and therapy
records ( Holt et al., 2021 ; OpenAPS community, 2026 ) . LLM-T1D distills a reinforcement-learning
policy into a language model that doses insulin and explains its
decisions ( Sarkar, 2026 ) .
blocks.zh:
以规则为基础的葡萄糖控制器组织在结构化葡萄糖和疗法周围进行注射
(Holt等,2021年;OpenAPS社区,2026年). LLM-T1D 衍射出增强学习
政策化为一种对胰岛素进行剂量和解释的语言模型
裁决(Sarkar,2026年)

blocks.en:
We instantiate APC for glucose control in type 1 diabetes, combining device observations
with contextual reports and personal experience. The state comprises glucose, insulin
still acting, carbohydrate absorption, and device
status; meals, activity, and illness perturb this state. APC observes sensor
or meter readings, delivery logs and alarms, and reports of meals, activity, and device
problems. Its actions are insulin delivery through boluses, temporary basal rates,
or injections, measurement requests such as scans and fingersticks, device management such as
cancellation, suspension, and resumption, and waiting. The score combines time in
range, hypoglycemia, and variability of true glucose (Section 4.2 ; Battelino et al., 2019 ). The idealized reference is a healthy pancreas, which regulates glucose continuously without
devices or reports.

blocks.en: 3 DiabetSim
blocks.zh: 3 糖尿病

blocks.en:
DiabetSim is a configurable environment for virtual testing of glucose-control agents.
It comprises a physiological engine, monitoring and delivery device models, and an
instance generator. Together, these components simulate individual glucose responses,
everyday events, and device-mediated interventions. Agents observe device readings and
event reports; the evaluator records the underlying glucose trajectory for scoring.

DiabetSim是一种可虚拟测试葡萄糖控制剂的可配置环境.
它包括一个生动发动机、监测和运载工具模型和一个
实例生成器。 这些组件共同模拟了单个葡萄糖反应,
日常活动,以及由设备调解的干预。 特工观察设备读取和
事件报告; 评价者记录葡萄糖的基本轨迹,以便打分。

blocks.en: 3.1 Simulator Engine
blocks.zh: 3.1 模拟引擎

blocks.en:
The engine models glucose–insulin dynamics using Deichmann et al. (2023) , including the
effects of physical activity. Individual parameters θ \theta specify insulin sensitivity
and body-mass-dependent responses. The simulator includes eight physiological
types with different body masses and dawn phenomena, together with day-to-day variation
in insulin sensitivity. Meals introduce carbohydrate absorption, while activity and
illness modify subsequent physiological responses. The simulator configures therapy settings
separately from physiological parameters, allowing prescribed treatment to differ from
an individual’s insulin requirements. An event-driven scheduler advances physiological
and device states as external events occur and treatment actions execute.

与生理参数分开,允许规定治疗方法不同于
个人的胰岛素要求。 一个事件驱动的调度器推进了生理
并按外部事件的发生和处理行动执行。

blocks.en: 3.2 Devices
blocks.zh: 3.2 设备

blocks.en:
Observation. Monitoring devices determine the measurements available to the agent.
The simulator includes eight sensor models and six glucose-meter models,
parameterized by published accuracy specifications ( Vettoretti et al., 2019 ; International Organization for Standardization, 2013 ) .
Real-time continuous glucose monitors (CGMs) produce readings every five minutes;
flash sensors return readings upon scanning, and meters upon fingerstick measurement.
The models represent sensor warm-up, data gaps, and compression artifacts. Scans and
fingerstick measurements are agent actions, making observation timing part of the control
policy. A reporting configuration ρ \rho additionally specifies the availability, timing,
and accuracy of reports about meals, activity, and other events.

blocks.en:
Action set. Delivery devices determine the available treatment operations and
their constraints. The simulator includes five pump models, 10 pen models,
and 10 insulin formulations. Each device configuration d d defines an action
set 𝒜 d \mathcal{A}_{d} : pumps support device-specific subsets of boluses, temporary basal
rates, extended boluses, cancellation, and suspension or resumption; pens support discrete
injections. Insulin formulations determine the corresponding absorption and action profiles.
The device interface validates commands against dose increments, dose limits, bolus intervals,
and device state, and records rejected commands with their reasons. Occlusions and suspension alter
actual delivery, separating the requested intervention from the dose received.

blocks.en: 3.3 Instance Generation
blocks.zh: 3.3 实例生成

blocks.en:
An instance specifies patient parameters, device and reporting configurations,
the event schedule, initial physiological and device states, pre-episode
history, evaluation horizon, and random seed. The generator assigns representative parameter values
or samples from configured ranges, then combines these specifications to produce
instances with different patients, devices, events, and observation conditions. Event
combinations, timing, and magnitude are configurable independently of the patient and
device parameters. Saving the resolved specification fixes the initialization, external
event schedule, and random seed for replay and comparisons between controllers.

blocks.en: 5.1 Setting

blocks.en:
Protocol. We evaluate all methods on the 212 tasks of SweetBench . Each 72-hour episode fixes the patient, initial state, event calendar, and
random seed, and uses a simulated Dana-i pump, insulin aspart, and real-time CGM under I2.
Meals and other events remain unreported. Each method acts through the same device
interface using only visible measurements and records; the environment continues to
evolve between decisions. The main evaluation adds no separate background HCL controller.
We compute COGI and its three subscores from 864 five-minute true-glucose samples per
episode, then average completed episodes with equal weight (Section 4.2 ).

and micro-boluses from glucose feedback. All three controllers use 15-minute decision
intervals and the same visible observations. Appendix C.2 specifies the
formulas, rules, and OpenAPS implementation; the case studies also use OpenAPS as their reference.

blocks.en: 5.3.1 Does Personal Experience Improve Control?
blocks.zh: 5.3.1 个人经验是否改善控制?

blocks.en:
We test whether personal records and end-of-day review improve control across days.
On six configurations over seven days, we compare four conditions: daily record reset , which passes no personal record to the next day; cross-day record only , which retains personal records for the next day without
additional end-of-day review; record + review-generated plan , which retains
records and reviews the day’s treatment responses to generate a plan for subsequent
control; and record + plan + execution feedback , which additionally incorporates
feedback on the execution of previous plans into the review. All conditions reset the
conversation daily while maintaining continuous physiology and fixed model weights.

blocks.en:
We compare pens and DASH with CL off or on in Slow-Meal Overlap, Stress Resolution,
and Post-Illness Refeeding, testing both delivery options and cooperation with a
background controller. Each configuration uses the same agent for a 72-hour run in
each case. DASH-w/o CL scores approximately 6–8 points above pens, mainly through time
in range and variability (Table 5 ). Turning CL on further raises
COGI by 4.63 and 2.53 points in the first two cases and gives a similar score in the
third, without increasing the agent’s decision frequency. The background HCL supplies
frequent basal-rate adjustments, while the agent integrates observations and personal
history to choose doses, carbohydrate intake, and device actions. The trajectories show
how adjustable infusion follows prolonged absorption and changing insulin needs
(Figure 4 ). These cases show that delivery configurations
shape control performance and support the potential of high-frequency closed-loop
control combined with lower-frequency agent decisions.

blocks.en: 5.3.3 How Do Information and Decision Frequency Affect Control?
blocks.zh: 5.3.3 信息和决定频率如何影响控制?

blocks.en:
We test the effects of information and decision frequency in Infusion-Site Leakage and
Mixed-Intensity Exercise. Each scenario crosses three information levels with fixed
intervals of 15, 30, 60, and 120 minutes, giving 24 runs of 72 hours each with the same
extra-decision allowance. At a fixed 60-minute interval, moving from I2 to I0 raises COGI
by 43.2 points on leakage and 15.7 on exercise (Table 6 ). Under I2,
shortening the interval from 120 to 15 minutes adds 10.5 and 3.7 points, respectively.
Averaged over both scenarios and all information levels, input-token use at 15 minutes
is about 4.2 times that at 60 minutes. In these two cases, added context yields larger
gains than increasing frequency alone. Frequent decisions partly compensate for missing
information but require more computation. Together with the CL-on/off results and the
interval sweep for OpenAPS (Appendix C.2 ), this supports using frequent
background control alongside an agent that makes informed, less frequent decisions.

In C04, a 39-year-old woman skips breakfast and lunch and exercises repeatedly for long periods
before a late meal, so hypoglycemia is a constant risk. APC scores 85.06 against 77.73 for
OpenAPS ( + 7.33 +7.33 ). Its time in 4–8 mmol/L is 84.14%, slightly below OpenAPS’s 85.42%, but
its time below 70 mg/dL is 2.55%, compared with 6.13% for OpenAPS.
Figure 5 marks three decisions. At marker 1 (10.58 h), a meter check
confirms a low of 67 mg/dL and the agent gives 12 g of fast carbohydrate. As glucose keeps
falling with little insulin recorded as active, the agent’s rationale raises the possibility of
unreported exercise, and it responds with carbohydrate and temporary basal
reductions that it can later reverse. At marker 2 (58 h), its record of low glucose in the late
morning on the two previous days leads it to lower the temporary basal rate to 20% early, and
it adds carbohydrate at 58.42 and 58.58 h as glucose continues to drop. At marker 3 (68 h),
having seen a strong fall after an earlier correction, it gives only 0.7 U, and when glucose
falls faster than it predicted, it lowers basal delivery again. In this episode the agent checks
the sensor against the meter, revises its explanation when the response does not match, and
carries lessons from earlier days into later doses.

In E04, an adolescent girl has recurring infusion-site leakage and intermittent positive sensor
drift. APC scores 47.37 against 66.20 for OpenAPS ( − 18.83 -18.83 ), with 10.65% of the time in
4–8 mmol/L and no true glucose below 70 mg/dL, so the deficit comes from persistent
hyperglycemia and high variability. Near marker 1 in Figure 7 , the agent uses
meter checks and calibration to detect the sensor disagreement, but it repeatedly attributes the
weak response to insulin to unreported food or changing insulin needs. It changes the infusion
set at 13 h (marker 2), about 12.75 h after the leak began, and the saved simulator state
confirms that effective delivery then recovers from 15% to 100%. When the leak returns near
24.17 h and 48.33 h, however, it does not change the set again. At marker 3 (50 h), with CGM at
its upper display limit, it gives another 2.5 U. Over the episode it requests 60 boluses, of
which 59 are delivered and one is rejected by the minimum-interval rule, and it changes the set
only once. The agent found the fault once but did not test that explanation again when the same
symptoms returned, and it kept adding insulin instead of looking for the cause.

blocks.en: 6 Discussion
blocks.zh: 讨论

blocks.en: 6.1 Decision Making under Incomplete Information
blocks.zh: 6.1 在不完全资料之下作出决定

blocks.en:
The information ablation identifies an opportunity to improve how agents combine
measurements, event context, and personal history. Added context improves control more
than increasing decision frequency alone in the tested cases. Explicit uncertainty
estimates and targeted measurement requests could help the agent distinguish changing
insulin needs from delivery or sensor problems. Personal records can retain these
inferences and guide later reassessment.

blocks.en: 6.2 Safety
blocks.zh: 6.2 安全问题

blocks.en:
Insulin continues to act after delivery, making dose history and reassessment timing
central to physiological control ( Holt et al., 2021 ) . Dose limits, insulin-on-board
estimation, and low-glucose monitoring provide concrete opportunities for improving agent
design. The CL-on/off cases also motivate combining frequent background regulation with
less frequent agent decisions. Separate hypoglycemia scores and action records support
assessment of these designs alongside overall control performance.

估计和低葡萄糖监测为改进剂提供了具体的机会

blocks.en: 6.3 Sim2Real Gap
blocks.zh: 6.3 Sim2 实际差距

blocks.en:
Patient-specific reconstruction offers a path to improving simulator fidelity.
Real CGM and device records can inform physiology, sensor errors, and event patterns;
held-out records can then assess the reconstructed environment. A Real2Sim2Real cycle
would let the agent develop a strategy in that environment and refine both the strategy
and the environment as further patient observations become available.

blocks.en: 9 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 9 结论

blocks.en:
We introduce DiabAgent , comprising the APC framework, the DiabetSim simulator, and the SweetBench benchmark. APC links agent decisions to medical-device actions and applies this control loop to glucose management in type 1 diabetes. DiabetSim provides virtual testing across patients, events, devices, and observation conditions. SweetBench turns this environment into 212 tasks for evaluating the physiological outcomes of agent decisions.
Together, these components establish a reproducible research setting for agentic physiological control.
We hope DiabAgent provides a foundation for agents to participate in human physiological control and supports extending this research to other physiological systems.
blocks.zh:
我们介绍DiabAgent, 包括APC框架、DiabetSim模拟器和Sweet Bench基准。 APC将代理决定与医疗设备行动联系起来,并将这一控制循环应用于1型糖尿病的葡萄糖管理. DiabetSim提供跨患者,事件,设备,和观察条件的虚拟测试. Sweet Bench将这种环境转化为212项任务,用于评价代理决策的生理结果.
这些成分共同建立了可再生的研究环境,用于剂性生理控制.
我们希望DiabAgent为物剂参与人类生理控制提供基础,并支持将这一研究扩展到其他生理系统.
